questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Which part do we see with?
questions.explanation: We see with our eyes. Ears are for hearing and the nose is for smelling.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: We smell with our ___.
questions.explanation: We smell with our nose. Breathe in and sniff a flower!

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Match each part to what it finds out.
questions.explanation: Eyes see colours, ears hear sounds, a nose smells flowers and a tongue tastes a sour lemon.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Which part do we taste with?
questions.explanation: We taste with our tongue. It tells us if food is sweet or sour.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Scientists ask questions.
questions.explanation: Yes! Scientists ask "What is it?" and "What will happen if…?" Asking questions helps us learn.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Rafi wants to see a tiny ant. Which tool helps?
questions.explanation: A magnifying glass makes small things look bigger, so we can look closely.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Tap all the tools a scientist uses.
questions.explanation: Scientists look closely with a magnifying glass, measure with a ruler and check how hot things are with a thermometer. A lollipop and a teddy are not tools.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Feel and sort. Is it soft or hard?
questions.explanation: A sponge, a teddy and wool are soft and squishy. A brick, a rock and a spoon are hard.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Put the science steps in order.
sequence: Ask a question
Make a guess
Try it out
Look at what happened
questions.explanation: A scientist asks a question, makes a guess, tries it out, and then looks to see what happened.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Which one will float in water?
questions.explanation: Wood floats on water. A key and a coin are heavy for their size, so they sink.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Tap all the things that float.
questions.explanation: A leaf, a ball and wood float on water. A rock, a key and a coin sink. Try it in a bowl of water to check!

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Rafi guessed a key would float. It sank. His guess was wrong.
questions.explanation: Yes. Scientists check their guess by trying it. Rafi saw the key sink, so his guess was wrong, and that is fine because we learn something.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Nadia finds a berry in the garden. What should she do?
questions.explanation: Only taste food that a grown-up gives you. Some berries are not safe to eat, so always ask a grown-up first.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Anika feels something in a bag. Which part helps her?
questions.explanation: We touch and feel with our hands. Our skin tells us if something is soft, hard, hot or cold.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: We heard 4 birds, 6 cars, 2 bells. Which was most?
questions.explanation: Count and compare: 6 is more than 4 and more than 2. We heard the most cars.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Put them in order, smallest to biggest.
questions.explanation: We compare things to see which is bigger. An ant is the smallest, then a mouse, a cat and an elephant is the biggest.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Match each tool to its job.
questions.explanation: A magnifying glass helps us look closely, a ruler measures, a camera takes a picture and a pencil draws what we see.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: We can draw a picture to show what we found.
questions.explanation: Yes. Scientists draw, take pictures and colour graphs so they can remember and tell others what they found.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Eyes shut, you shake a box. Which two parts help?
questions.explanation: Your hands feel the box shake and your ears hear the rattle. Your eyes are shut, so they cannot help.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Raju says the stone floats. Mina says it sinks. What next?
questions.explanation: We find out by trying it! Put the stone in water and look. Voting or guessing again cannot tell us what really happens.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: A dog is a living thing.
questions.explanation: Yes. A dog grows, eats, moves and has puppies, so it is living.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Sort the pictures. Living or non-living?
questions.explanation: Cats, fish, flowers and ants grow, need food or water, and make young. A teddy, a car, a chair and a rock were never alive.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Which one is a living thing?
questions.explanation: A tree grows, drinks water and makes seeds, so it is living. A rock and a chair do not grow.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Which one is a non-living thing?
questions.explanation: A car was never alive. It does not grow, eat or have babies. A fish and a flower are living.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: A plant needs water and ___ to grow.
questions.explanation: Plants drink water and need sunlight to grow. Toys and sweets are not food for plants.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: A rock can grow like a plant.
questions.explanation: No. A rock is non-living. It does not grow, eat or have babies. A plant grows from a tiny seed.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Tap all the things living things need.
questions.explanation: Living things need food, water, air, a home and care. A TV and a toy are fun, but we do not need them to live.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Match each baby to its grown-up.
questions.explanation: Living things grow up. A chick grows into a hen, a little plant grows into a tree and a baby grows into a grown-up.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Put Mina's seed story in order.
sequence: Mina plants a seed.
She gives it water and sun.
A green shoot comes up.
It grows into a sunflower.
questions.explanation: A seed in soil needs water and sunshine. It sends up a green shoot and slowly grows into a tall plant.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Mina's plant looks droopy and dry. What does it need?
questions.explanation: A dry, droopy plant needs water. Sweets and toys cannot help a plant.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Nadia has a kitten. Tap what the kitten needs.
questions.explanation: A kitten needs food, water and a safe, warm home, like all animals. A TV or a car is of no use to it.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Joy sees a strange bug. What should he do?
questions.explanation: Look with your eyes and do not touch bugs you do not know. Some can bite or sting. Wash your hands after exploring.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: What do we need to see cells?
questions.explanation: Cells are the tiny building blocks of living things. They are so small that we need a microscope to see them.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Living things are made of tiny ___.
questions.explanation: All living things are made of tiny parts called cells. Cells are so small we need a microscope to see them.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Which one can grow, eat and have babies?
questions.explanation: A cow grows, eats grass and has calves. A ball and a chair are non-living.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: We found 5 ants, 3 birds, 2 flowers. Which was most?
questions.explanation: Count and compare: 5 is more than 3 and more than 2. We found the most ants.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: A plant grows from a tiny seed.
questions.explanation: Yes. Plants are living things. A seed grows into a little plant and then a big plant.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: A toy car moves. A snail moves. Which one is living?
questions.explanation: Moving is not enough. A snail eats, grows and has babies. A toy car only moves when someone pushes it or it has a motor.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Put the chick pictures in order.
questions.explanation: A chick grows inside an egg. It hatches, is a fluffy chick, and then grows into a hen.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: A teddy bear is a living thing.
questions.explanation: No. A teddy bear does not eat, grow or have babies. It was never alive.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Match each animal to how it moves.
questions.explanation: Rabbits hop, birds fly, fish swim and snails slide along slowly. Animals move in different ways.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Tap all the animals that can fly.
questions.explanation: Birds have wings and feathers. Butterflies and bees are insects with wings, so they fly too. Fish swim and cows walk.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Which one is an animal?
questions.explanation: A duck is an animal. It moves, eats and has ducklings. A tree and a flower are plants.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Tap all the animals that live in water.
questions.explanation: Fish, crabs and dolphins live in water. Cats, cows and dogs live on land.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: An elephant uses its trunk to pick up food.
questions.explanation: Yes. An elephant uses its long trunk like a hand to pick up food and to drink water.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Sort the animals by how they move.
questions.explanation: Fish and dolphins swim. Birds and butterflies fly. Cats and cows walk or run on land.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Match each animal to what it gives us.
questions.explanation: Cows give us milk, hens give us eggs, bees make honey and sheep give us wool. Animals help us in many ways.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: A cow gives us ___ to drink.
questions.explanation: Cows give us milk. Hens give us eggs, bees make honey and sheep give us wool.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Put Nana's hen story in order.
sequence: The hen sits on her eggs.
Chicks come out of the eggs.
The chicks eat and grow.
The chicks become hens.
questions.explanation: A hen keeps her eggs warm. Chicks hatch, eat and grow bigger every day until they are hens too.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: A baby animal grows into a grown-up animal.
questions.explanation: Yes. Animal babies eat and grow bigger, just like you. A chick grows into a hen and a calf grows into a cow.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: A cow lays eggs.
questions.explanation: No. Hens lay eggs. A cow gives us milk.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Bees make honey.
questions.explanation: Yes. Honeybees make honey from flower nectar. Animals help us in many ways.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Look at the snail. How does it move?
questions.image_alt: A snail with a spiral shell.
questions.explanation: A snail slides along slowly on one soft foot. It cannot hop or fly.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: A bird lays its eggs in a ___.
questions.explanation: Birds build nests, often in trees. The mother bird keeps the eggs warm until the chicks hatch.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Tuli wears a woollen shawl. Which animal gave the wool?
questions.explanation: Sheep grow thick wool. People cut it, spin it into yarn and make warm clothes. Hens and fish do not have wool.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Sumi wants to see a fish. Where should she look?
questions.explanation: Fish live in water, in ponds, rivers and the sea. They breathe in the water and cannot live in trees or the sky.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Rafi sees a strange dog near the road. What should he do?
questions.explanation: Do not touch animals you do not know. Even a friendly looking dog may bite. Tell a grown-up.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: This is a chick. What will it grow into?
questions.image_alt: A baby chick.
questions.explanation: A chick grows into a hen. Baby animals grow into grown-ups of the same kind.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: I hop. I have long ears. Who am I?
questions.explanation: A rabbit hops on strong back legs and has long ears. A cat walks and a fish swims.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: A hen sits on 3 eggs. All hatch. How many chicks?
questions.explanation: Each egg hatches one chick. 3 eggs make 3 chicks.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Look at the plant. Which number is the flower?
questions.image_alt: A plant with a flower at the top, leaves, a stem, a fruit and roots under the ground, each marked with a number.
questions.explanation: Number 1 is the flower, at the top of the plant. Number 2 is a leaf and number 3 is the stem.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Which number shows the roots under the ground?
questions.image_alt: A plant with a flower at the top, leaves, a stem, a fruit and roots under the ground, each marked with a number.
questions.explanation: Number 4 is the roots. Roots grow under the ground.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Number 5 is the fruit.
questions.image_alt: A plant with a flower at the top, leaves, a stem, a fruit and roots under the ground, each marked with a number.
questions.explanation: Yes. Number 5 is the fruit. Fruits grow on plants and hold the seeds.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Match each word to its picture.
questions.explanation: Fruit, vegetables and rice all come from plants. Plants help us with our food.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Tap what a plant needs to grow.
questions.explanation: Plants need sunlight and water to grow. Sweets, ice cream and balls cannot help a plant grow.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Roots grow under the ___.
questions.explanation: Roots grow under the ground, in the soil. The leaves and flowers are above the ground.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Put the seed story in order.
sequence: A seed is in the soil.
A tiny shoot comes up.
Green leaves grow.
A flower opens.
questions.explanation: A seed in the soil gets water and warmth. A shoot comes up, leaves grow, and later the plant makes flowers.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Sort the plants.
questions.explanation: Palm and other trees are tall plants with a trunk. Roses and sunflowers are flowers. Carrots and broccoli are vegetables we eat.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Plants need water to grow.
questions.explanation: Yes. Plants drink water. They also need sunlight to grow well.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: A bean plant grows best in a dark cupboard.
questions.explanation: No. Without light a bean plant grows pale, thin and weak. It grows best by a window where there is light.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: A plant has roots under the ground.
questions.explanation: Yes. Roots grow under the ground. Leaves, flowers and fruit grow above it.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Moung's bean plant is under the bed. Where should it go?
questions.explanation: Plants need light. A window lets sunlight in, so the bean plant can grow green and strong.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Rafi is hot. Where can he sit in the shade?
questions.explanation: A big tree gives cool shade. Trees help us in many ways.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Grandpa's mango tree is big. Tap what it gives.
questions.explanation: A mango tree gives sweet fruit, cool shade and a safe home for birds. It does not give a car or a TV.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Which one is a fruit?
questions.explanation: An apple is a fruit. It grows on a tree and has seeds inside. Broccoli and potatoes are vegetables.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Which one is a baby plant?
questions.explanation: A seedling is a baby plant that has just grown from a seed. It will grow bigger.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: A seed grows into a ___.
questions.explanation: A tiny seed, with water and sunlight, grows into a plant.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Two beans: one in light, one in dark. Which grows strong?
questions.explanation: The bean in the light grows green and strong. The bean in the dark grows pale, thin and weak, because plants need light.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: A: sun. B: water. C: sun, water. Which grows best?
questions.explanation: Plants need both sunlight and water. C gets both, so it grows best.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Tap all the things plants give us.
questions.explanation: Mangoes, wood and carrots come from plants. Milk comes from cows and cars are made in factories.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Look at the body. Which number is the head?
questions.image_alt: A child with body parts marked by numbers: head, neck, shoulder, arm, elbow, hand, chest, tummy, leg, knee and foot.
questions.explanation: Number 1 is the head. Our eyes, ears, nose and mouth are on our head.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Which number is the hand?
questions.image_alt: A child with body parts marked by numbers: head, neck, shoulder, arm, elbow, hand, chest, tummy, leg, knee and foot.
questions.explanation: Number 6 is the hand. We use our hands to hold, touch and wave.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Which number is the knee?
questions.image_alt: A child with body parts marked by numbers: head, neck, shoulder, arm, elbow, hand, chest, tummy, leg, knee and foot.
questions.explanation: Number 10 is the knee. It bends in the middle of the leg. Number 5 is the elbow in the arm.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Match each part to its sense.
questions.explanation: Eyes see, ears hear, the nose smells, the tongue tastes and our skin and hands touch. These are our five senses.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Match each part to what it finds.
questions.explanation: Ears hear music, a nose smells a flower, a tongue tastes sweet honey and our hands feel cold ice.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Tap the parts we use to walk and run.
questions.explanation: We use our legs and our feet to walk and run. Ears are for hearing and eyes are for seeing.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Tuli wears glasses. Which sense do they help?
questions.explanation: Glasses help Tuli see clearly. Her eyes help her to read, play and learn.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: We hear with our ___.
questions.explanation: We hear with our ears. They help us enjoy music and know when someone calls us.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: We have five senses.
questions.explanation: Yes. We see, hear, smell, taste and touch. The five senses help us find out about the world.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Children are all exactly the same.
questions.explanation: No. We are the same in some ways, like having eyes and hands. We are different in our hair, height and clothes. That is what makes each of us special.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Put them in order, youngest to oldest.
questions.explanation: We start as a baby, grow into a child, then a grown-up, and later we become older.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Sort the body parts: head, arms or legs?
questions.explanation: Eyes, ears and nose are on our head. Hands and arms are together. Legs and feet help us walk.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Mina smells smoke in the kitchen. Which part tells her?
questions.explanation: Our nose smells smoke and warns us of danger. Mina should tell a grown-up straight away.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: How can Tuli look after her eyes?
questions.explanation: Tuli should wear her glasses and not sit too close to the TV. We should also never look at the Sun.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Mina smells and tastes a cake. Which two parts does she use?
questions.explanation: She smells the cake with her nose and tastes it with her tongue. Her foot cannot help and her ear is for hearing.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: You are bigger now than when you were a baby.
questions.explanation: Yes. Since you were born you have grown taller and stronger. Growing is a sign of being alive.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Tap what children have.
questions.explanation: Children have eyes, ears and hands. We are the same in many ways. What we wear or play with can be different.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: We feel hot and cold with our ___.
questions.explanation: Our skin helps us touch and feel things. It tells us if something is hot, cold, soft or rough.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: You hold your nose and taste a mango. What happens?
questions.explanation: Smell and taste work together. When you hold your nose, it is harder to taste.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: A cat has big ears. What can it do well?
questions.explanation: Animals use their senses too. A cat can hear small sounds, like a mouse moving.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Sort the foods. Every day or only a treat?
questions.explanation: Tomatoes, fish and rice are good to eat every day. Burgers, cake and lollipops are treats: just a little, not every day.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Which is the best drink when you are thirsty?
questions.explanation: Clean water is the best drink. Fizzy drinks are treats and sweets are not a drink.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Tap the healthy snacks.
questions.explanation: Bananas, carrots and apples are healthy snacks. Sweets, chips and doughnuts are treats.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Match each food to its group.
questions.explanation: Rice gives us energy to go. Fish helps us grow strong. Carrots help us glow and stay healthy. A lollipop is only a treat.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Go, grow or glow? Sort the foods.
questions.explanation: Go foods give us energy: rice and potato. Grow foods help us grow strong: fish and eggs. Glow foods keep us healthy: carrots and bananas.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: We drink clean ___ every day.
questions.explanation: Our body needs clean water every day to stay healthy.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Healthy food gives us energy to play.
questions.explanation: Yes. Food gives us energy to run and play, and it helps us grow.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Sweets are good to eat every day.
questions.explanation: No. Sweets, chips and fizzy drinks are treats. Eat just a little, and not every day.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Put Shopon's story in order.
sequence: Shopon eats chips and a fizzy drink.
He feels tired and hungry.
Mother packs roti, egg, banana and water.
Shopon has lots of energy to play.
questions.explanation: Chips and a fizzy drink left Shopon tired and hungry. A tiffin with roti, egg, banana and water gave him lots of energy.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Mother packs Shopon's tiffin. Which is best?
questions.explanation: A banana is a healthy fruit. Chips and doughnuts are treats, so they are not good for every day.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: It is Imran's birthday. How much cake is a good treat?
questions.explanation: Cake is a treat. A small piece is fine on a special day, but too much sugar is not good for our teeth or body.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Priya has rice for lunch. Which grow food can she add?
questions.explanation: Fish helps us grow strong. Rice is a go food, so adding fish makes a better meal. Sweets and lollipops are treats.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Tap the foods for a healthy lunch.
questions.explanation: Rice, fish and vegetables make a healthy lunch with go, grow and glow foods. Sweets and fizzy drinks are only treats.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Grow foods help us ___ strong.
questions.explanation: Fish, eggs, milk and dal are grow foods. They help our body grow strong.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Favourite fruit: mango 6, banana 4, apple 2. Which is most?
questions.explanation: Count and compare: 6 is more than 4 and more than 2. Mango is the favourite.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Which one is only a treat?
questions.explanation: A lollipop is a treat. We eat just a little, not every day. Apples and carrots are healthy.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: We should drink clean water every day.
questions.explanation: Yes. Water keeps our body healthy. It is the best drink.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Roti is Go. Egg is Grow. Which Glow food can we add?
questions.explanation: An apple is a glow food. Roti, an egg and an apple make a balanced meal. Doughnuts and cookies are treats.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Which lunch has go, grow and glow foods?
questions.explanation: Rice is go, fish is grow and carrot is glow, so that lunch has all three. The first lunch has only go foods and the last has only treats.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Tap the foods that give us energy to go.
questions.explanation: Rice, roti and potato are go foods. They give us energy to play. Eggs help us grow and carrots help us glow.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Sort the pictures. Day or night?
questions.explanation: We see the sunrise, the Sun and go to school in the day. At night we see stars and the Moon, and we sleep in bed.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Which one do we see in the sky at night?
questions.explanation: We see the Moon and the stars in the night sky. The Sun shines in the day.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Match the weather to what we need.
questions.explanation: We use an umbrella in the rain, cool water when it is sunny and hot, a warm scarf when it is cold, and a kite when it is windy.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Rain is falling. What should Mina take to school?
questions.explanation: An umbrella keeps the rain off. Ice cream and a ball do not help in the rain.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: At night, we can see the Moon and the ___.
questions.explanation: At night the sky is dark and we may see the Moon and the stars.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Put the times of the day in order.
questions.explanation: The day starts with the morning, then comes the bright day, and then it is night.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: In the day, the ___ lights up our sky.
questions.explanation: The Sun gives us light in the day. At night it is dark.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: The Sun shines at night.
questions.explanation: No. The Sun shines in the day. At night the sky is dark and we may see the Moon and stars.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Tap the pictures that show weather.
questions.explanation: Sunny, rainy and windy are kinds of weather. A bed and a school are not weather.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: The Sun shines on this side. Is it day or night?
questions.image_alt: The Sun on the left shines on the Earth. The side facing the Sun is marked DAY and the dark side is marked NIGHT.
questions.explanation: It is day on the side of the Earth that faces the Sun. The other side is dark, so it is night there.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Which one is the full Moon?
questions.explanation: The full Moon is the big, round, bright Moon. A thin Moon looks like a smile, and a new Moon is dark.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: In 10 days: 5 sunny, 3 cloudy, 2 rainy. Which was most?
questions.explanation: Count and compare: 5 is more than 3 and more than 2. There were most sunny days.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: It is a cool winter morning. Tap what Priya can wear.
questions.explanation: In the cool season we wear warm clothes like a coat and a scarf. An umbrella is for rain and a ball is for play.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Mitu wants to see the thin new Moon. When should she look?
questions.explanation: We can see the Moon at night, when the sky is dark. Mitu's family looks for the thin new Moon to know when Eid begins.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Windy days are good for flying kites.
questions.explanation: Yes. The wind lifts a kite up high. A calm day makes it hard to fly a kite.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Match each season to what it is like.
questions.explanation: In Bangladesh, summer is hot, the rainy season has lots of rain and winter is cool.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: The seasons come back every year.
questions.explanation: Yes. Summer, the rainy season and winter come again and again. This is a pattern we can count on.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Example: sunny, cloudy, rainy, sunny, cloudy. What comes next?
questions.explanation: Look for the pattern: sunny, cloudy, rainy, then it starts again. After cloudy comes rainy.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: It is noon, but dark clouds fill the sky. Is it night?
questions.explanation: Clouds can make the day look dark, but the Sun is still in the sky at noon, so it is day.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: The Moon looks a little different from night to night.
questions.explanation: Yes. Some nights the Moon is a thin smile and some nights it is round and bright.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Sort the places. Natural or built by people?
questions.explanation: Forests, rivers and hills are natural places. Houses, schools and cities are built by people.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Which place is natural?
questions.explanation: A hill is a natural place. Nature made it. A school and a hospital are built by people.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Which place is built by people?
questions.explanation: People build houses to live in. A river and a hill are natural places.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Tap the things we get from nature.
questions.explanation: We get water, wood and fish from nature. A car and a TV are made by people in factories.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Match each old thing to its new use.
questions.explanation: We can reuse old things. A tin can makes a pencil pot, a bottle makes a plant pot and a box makes a toy car.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: We put rubbish in the ___.
questions.explanation: Rubbish goes in the bin. It must not go on the ground or in the river.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Reduce, reuse and ___ to help our Earth.
questions.explanation: Reduce means use less, reuse means use again, and recycle means make old things into new things.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: A river is a natural place.
questions.explanation: Yes. Nature made rivers. People did not build them.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Rubbish in the river is good for fish.
questions.explanation: No. Rubbish makes the water dirty and fish cannot live there. Keep our river clean.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Put the river clean-up story in order.
sequence: Children see rubbish in the river.
They pick it up and put it in bags.
The river is clean again.
They put up a "Keep our river clean" sign.
questions.explanation: The children saw rubbish in the river, picked it up with their teachers, and then the river was clean. Then they put up a sign.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Mina has an empty bottle. Where does it go?
questions.explanation: Rubbish goes in the bin. In the river it would hurt the fish and make the water dirty.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Nadia goes shopping. What can she take to carry things?
questions.explanation: A cloth bag can be used again and again, so we use less plastic.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Joy wants to help nature. What is a good idea?
questions.explanation: Planting a tree is kind to nature. Trees give shade, food and homes for birds. Rubbish and wasted water hurt nature.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Sort the actions. Kind to nature or hurts nature?
questions.explanation: Binning rubbish, taking a cloth bag and planting a tree are kind. Spilling oil, dirty smoke and bottles on the ground hurt nature.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Which one makes the air dirty?
questions.explanation: Smoke from a factory makes the air dirty. A growing tree makes the air cleaner, and a cloth bag makes no smoke.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Match each word to what it means.
questions.explanation: Reduce means use less. Reuse means use it again. Recycle means make old things into new things.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: This place was built by people.
questions.image_alt: A hospital building.
questions.explanation: Yes. A hospital is a building that people built to help sick people get better.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Which is the best thing to do with an old bottle?
options: Use it as a plant pot
questions.explanation: We can reuse a bottle as a plant pot. Throwing it in the river or on the road makes a mess and hurts nature.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Children throw rubbish in a river. What can happen to fish?
questions.explanation: Rubbish makes the water dirty, so fish can get sick and cannot live there. Our choices can hurt living things.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: We get fish and wood from nature.
questions.explanation: Yes. Fish live in rivers and the sea, and wood comes from trees. We use many things from nature.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: Which one can hurt us?
questions.explanation: Fire is hot and can burn us. A teddy bear and a ball are safe to play with.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: Tap the things that can hurt us.
questions.explanation: Fire, sockets and sharp knives can hurt us, so we keep away. A teddy bear and a ball are safe toys.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: Sort the pictures. Play with it or keep away?
questions.explanation: We play with toys like a teddy bear, a ball and crayons. We keep away from fire, knives and sockets.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: The light is red. What does Mina do?
questions.explanation: A red light means stop. Mina stops and waits for green before she goes.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: Match each sign to what it says.
questions.explanation: A stop sign says stop. A warning sign says take care. A traffic light says wait for green. A bin sign says use the bin.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: We put rubbish in the ___.
questions.explanation: Rubbish goes in the bin. It does not go in the river or under a tree.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: Which one helps keep our hands clean?
questions.explanation: Soap and water wash germs and dirt off our hands. Sweets and crayons do not clean us.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: Tap what helps keep us clean.
questions.explanation: Soap, a broom and a toothbrush help keep us and our places clean. A lollipop does not clean anything.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: A clean place has no rubbish on the floor.
questions.explanation: A clean place has no rubbish and smells fresh.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: Danger! Put what we do in order.
questions.explanation: First we stop. Then we keep away. Last we tell a grown-up, who can help.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: Ayaan sees a hot pan. What should he do?
questions.explanation: A hot pan can burn us. Ayaan keeps away from the stove.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: Raju has an empty can. Where should it go?
questions.image_alt: A tin can.
questions.explanation: Empty cans go in the bin. Rubbish in a river or under a tree makes the place dirty.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: Tuli finds some medicine. What should she do?
questions.image_alt: A pill.
questions.explanation: Medicine can be dangerous if we take it by ourselves. Tuli tells a grown-up.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: Nadia waits for the green light before she crosses.
questions.explanation: We wait for the green light and look both ways before we cross.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: A hot pan can burn us.
questions.explanation: Hot pans and stoves can burn us, so we keep away.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: Example: 4 papers, 3 bottles, 2 cans. Which was most?
questions.explanation: Count each one. There were 4 papers, which is more than 3 bottles or 2 cans.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: A ball rolls onto the road. What should Joy do?
questions.explanation: Joy should stop and ask a grown-up. Running onto the road is dangerous.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: We can play with plugs and sockets.
questions.explanation: Plugs and sockets use strong electricity and can hurt us. We never play with them.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: If something looks dangerous, tell a ___.
questions.explanation: When we see danger, we keep away and tell a grown-up.

questions.title: Clean and Safe Spaces
questions.stem: Mina is by deep water. She stays with a grown-up.
questions.explanation: Deep water is a danger. Staying with a grown-up keeps us safe.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: What is a pencil made of?
questions.image_alt: A pencil.
questions.explanation: A pencil is made of wood. Wood comes from trees.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: Match each thing to its material.
questions.explanation: A chair is made of wood, a key of metal, socks of cloth and a bottle of plastic.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: Sort the pictures. Hard or soft?
questions.explanation: A stone, a key and a brick feel hard. A teddy bear, socks and yarn feel soft.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: Mina needs a raincoat. Which material keeps rain out?
questions.explanation: Plastic keeps rain out. Paper gets soggy and wool soaks up water.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: Which one can we see through?
questions.explanation: We can see through clear glass. We cannot see through wood or brick.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: Tap the things made of metal.
questions.explanation: A key, a coin and a nut and bolt are made of metal. Socks are cloth and a teddy bear is cloth too.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: Everything is made of a material.
questions.explanation: Every thing around us is made of one or more materials, like wood, plastic, metal, glass, paper or cloth.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: A teddy is made of ___.
questions.explanation: Most teddy bears are made of soft cloth.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: Which one feels hard?
questions.explanation: A stone feels hard. A teddy bear and socks feel soft.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: Put the house story in order.
questions.explanation: First the friends build houses. Then a strong wind comes. At the end only the brick house is still standing.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: A strong wind is coming. Which house is safest?
questions.explanation: The brick house stayed up in the story. Bricks are strong, but paper and sticks are blown away or fall down.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: Tia says a paper house is strong in a big wind.
questions.explanation: Paper is weak. A strong wind blew the paper house away.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: Plastic can keep rain out.
questions.explanation: Plastic is waterproof, so raincoats are often made of it.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: A key is made of ___.
questions.explanation: Keys are made of metal. Metal is hard.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: Tap the words for how a material feels.
questions.explanation: Soft, rough and smooth tell us how a material feels when we touch it. Loud is about sound.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: Example: 5 wood, 3 plastic, 2 metal things. Which was most?
questions.explanation: Count each group. Wood has 5, which is more than 3 or 2.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: Key, coin, spoon: hard and shiny. What are they made of?
questions.explanation: Keys, coins and spoons are all hard and shiny. They are made of metal.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: We can see through a wooden door.
questions.explanation: Wood is not clear, so we cannot see through it. We can see through clear glass.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: Sort the pictures. Wood or metal?
questions.explanation: Chairs, pencils and doors are made of wood. Keys, spoons and coins are made of metal.

questions.title: Materials Around Us
questions.stem: Tuli uses a plastic bucket to carry water.
questions.explanation: A plastic bucket can hold water and does not soak it up.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.stem: Sort the pictures. Push or pull?
questions.explanation: We push a ball when we kick it, push a door shut and push a trolley. We pull a kite string, pull a bucket rope and a tractor pulls a trailer.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.stem: Which one do we push?
questions.explanation: We push a trolley away from us. We pull a kite string and a bucket rope towards us.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.stem: Which one shows a pull?
questions.explanation: Pulling up a bucket on a rope is a pull. Kicking a ball and shutting a door are pushes.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.stem: A push moves something away from you.
questions.explanation: A push moves things away from us. A pull moves things towards us.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.stem: A pull moves something towards you.
questions.explanation: A pull brings things closer to us, like pulling a cart or a kite string.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.stem: Opening a drawer is a ___.
questions.explanation: We pull a drawer towards us to open it.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.subskill: What pushes and pulls can do
questions.stem: Match what we do to what happens.
questions.explanation: Kicking a still ball starts it moving. Catching a rolling ball stops it. Pedalling harder makes a bicycle go faster.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.stem: Put the boat story in order.
questions.explanation: The boat comes back from the river. Then the people push and pull it. At the end it is up on the bank.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.stem: Which will roll down a slope?
questions.explanation: A ball is round, so it rolls down a slope. A flat book or a box slides but does not roll.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.stem: Mina wants her toy car to go faster. What can she do?
questions.explanation: A bigger push makes the car go faster. A small push makes it go slowly and holding it makes it stop.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.stem: A push from a friend makes Tuli's swing go faster.
questions.explanation: A push can make something go faster, like a swing.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.stem: Tap how the people move the heavy boat.
questions.explanation: The people pulled the rope and pushed the back of the boat. Sleeping and eating do not move a boat.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.subskill: Pushes and pulls in a simulation
questions.stem: The cart stays still when both teams pull the same.

sim.task: Open Forces and Motion: Basics and choose Net Force. Put one small puller on the blue rope on the left and one small puller on the red rope on the right. Press Go and watch the cart.

questions.explanation: When both sides pull with the same strength, the pulls cancel out and the cart does not move.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.subskill: Pushes and pulls in a simulation
questions.stem: Which way does the cart go?

sim.task: Open Forces and Motion: Basics and choose Net Force. Put one small puller on the blue rope on the left. Put two small pullers on the red rope on the right. Press Go and watch the cart.

questions.explanation: Two pullers pull harder than one puller. The cart goes to the red side where there are more pullers.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.stem: Which animal can pull a cart?
questions.explanation: A cow or a water buffalo is strong and can pull a cart. Fish and owls cannot.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.stem: Example: car 7 tiles, bus 4, rickshaw 5. Which went farthest?
questions.explanation: Compare the numbers. The red car rolled 7 tiles, which is more than 5 or 4.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.subskill: What pushes and pulls can do
questions.stem: A ball starts to roll. A push or pull made it.
questions.explanation: Things do not start moving by themselves. A push or a pull makes them move.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.subskill: What pushes and pulls can do
questions.stem: A push can make a ball do what?
questions.explanation: A push can make a ball roll, speed up, slow down or change direction. It cannot make a ball sing or grow.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.stem: Tap the things we push.
questions.explanation: We push a trolley and we push a ball when we kick it. We pull a kite string and a bucket rope.

questions.title: Pushes and Pulls
questions.subskill: What pushes and pulls can do
questions.stem: A push can make a moving thing stop.
questions.explanation: A push can stop something, like a hand stopping a rolling ball.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.stem: Tap the things that give light.
questions.explanation: The Sun, a candle and a torch give out light. A teddy bear and a ball do not.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.stem: Sort the pictures. Makes light or makes sound?
questions.explanation: Fire, stars and a lamp make light. A barking dog, a drum and a bell make sound.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.stem: Which part of us hears sounds?
questions.explanation: We hear sounds with our ears. Eyes are for seeing.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.stem: Match each instrument to how we play it.
questions.explanation: We hit a drum, pluck the strings of a guitar and shake maracas. Each way makes a different sound.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.stem: The Sun gives us light.
questions.explanation: The Sun is our biggest light source. It lights up the day.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.stem: A bell sounds quieter when we are far away.
questions.explanation: Sound gets fainter as it travels away from the bell.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.stem: Babu is in the dark. What gives him light?
questions.explanation: A torch gives out light, so Babu can see. A teddy bear and a ball give no light.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.stem: Mina walks away from the school bell. The sound gets...
questions.explanation: The farther we are from a sound, the quieter it is.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.subskill: Light and sound in daily life
questions.stem: Put the power cut story in order.
questions.explanation: First the lights go out. Then Father switches on a torch. Now Babu can see his toys.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.stem: We hear sounds with our ___.
questions.explanation: We hear when sound goes into our ears.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.stem: A drum makes sound when we ___ it.
questions.explanation: Hitting the drum makes a sound.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.stem: How do we play a flute?
questions.image_alt: A flute.
questions.explanation: We blow into a flute. We hit a drum and shake a shaker.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.stem: Which one makes a sound when we shake it?
questions.explanation: A shaker makes a sound when we shake it. A candle and a torch do not.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.stem: Tap the ways to make a sound.
questions.explanation: We can hit a drum, clap or blow a flute to make sounds. Sleeping makes no sound.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.stem: A teddy bear gives out light.
questions.explanation: A teddy bear is not a light source. It does not give out light.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.subskill: Light and sound in daily life
questions.stem: Only a grown-up should light a candle.
questions.explanation: Candles have fire, which can burn us. Only a grown-up lights a candle.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.subskill: Light and sound in daily life
questions.stem: We can look straight at the Sun.
questions.explanation: Looking straight at the Sun can hurt our eyes. We never do it.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.stem: Example: more boxes = louder. Rice 3, dal 5, stones 8. Loudest?
questions.explanation: Count the boxes. Stones have 8, which is more than 5 or 3, so stones were loudest.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.stem: Babu hears a quiet bell. How can he hear it louder?
questions.explanation: A sound is louder when we are closer to it. Walking away makes it quieter.

questions.title: Light and Sound
questions.stem: Which gives light in the night sky?
questions.explanation: Stars give out light in the night sky, like tiny faraway suns. A kite and a bird do not.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: A hand lens helps you see small things closely.
questions.explanation: A hand lens makes small things look bigger. We use it to look closely at a leaf, an ant or a seed.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Match each tool to its job.
questions.explanation: A ruler measures length. A hand lens helps us look closely. A thermometer shows how hot or cold. A timer shows how long something takes.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Put the steps in order. What does a scientist do first? Then?
sequence: Ask a question.
Guess what will happen.
Test it.
Record what happens.
Tell others.
questions.explanation: A scientist asks a question, makes a guess, tests it, records what happens and then tells other people.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: To find which ball bounces highest, we drop every ball from the same height.
questions.explanation: Dropping every ball from the same height makes the test fair. Then only the ball is different.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: In a fair test, we keep things the ___.
questions.explanation: In a fair test we keep things the same. We only change one thing.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: How do young scientists stay safe? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: We listen to our teacher, wash our hands and ask before we smell anything. We never taste things in a test, and we do not run around.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Which tool would you use? Sort each job.
items: how tall a bean plant is
how long sand takes to fall
questions.explanation: A ruler measures length and height. A thermometer measures how hot or cold. A timer measures how long something takes.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Before the test, Mina says: 'I think the rubber ball will bounce highest.' What is this?
questions.explanation: A prediction is a good guess about what will happen. A result is what we see after the test.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Look at the thermometers. Which one shows the hottest?
questions.image_alt: Three thermometers A, B and C. A is at 12 degrees, B at 37 degrees and C at 48 degrees.
questions.explanation: The red line goes highest on thermometer C. A higher line means hotter.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Which tool measures how long a book is?
questions.explanation: A ruler measures how long something is. The stopwatch is for time, the thermometer is for how hot, and the balance scale is for how heavy.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Sort the tools. Which ones measure? Which ones help you look closely?
questions.explanation: Rulers, thermometers and stopwatches give us numbers. Hand lenses and microscopes make tiny things easier to see.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Look at the thermometers. Put them in order from hottest to coldest.
questions.image_alt: Three thermometers A, B and C. A shows 5 degrees, B shows 25 degrees and C shows 40 degrees.
sequence: thermometer C
thermometer B
thermometer A
questions.explanation: The line is highest on C, so C is the hottest. B is in the middle. The line is lowest on A, so A is the coldest.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Nadia drew these pictures each week. The tadpoles grew into frogs.
questions.image_alt: Life cycle of a frog: eggs, tadpole, froglet, adult frog.
questions.explanation: Nadia looked closely and drew what she saw. The picture shows eggs, then tadpoles, then froglets, then adult frogs.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Which part of your body helps you see what a leaf looks like?
questions.explanation: We use our eyes to see. Looking closely is one way to find out about things.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Mina and Raju race toy cars down a ramp. Mina pushes her car. Raju lets his car go. Is it a fair test?
options: No. Mina pushed her car and Raju did not.
Yes. Both cars are on the same ramp.
Yes. Both children are in Class 1.
questions.explanation: Mina pushed, so her car got a head start. A fair race lets both cars go the same way.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Nadia sees tiny black wriggly things in the village pond. What does a young scientist do?
options: Guess a name and stop looking.
Look closely and draw what she sees.
questions.explanation: Scientists look closely and record what they see. We never taste things to find out, and one guess is not enough.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: At home, Joy finds a bottle of coloured liquid in the kitchen. He wants to know what it is. What is the safe choice?
options: Ask a grown-up and do not touch it.
questions.explanation: Some liquids are dangerous. We ask a grown-up and never smell, taste or touch things we do not know.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Tuli wants to know how tall her bean plant is. She measures it with a ___.
questions.explanation: A ruler measures how tall or how long something is.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Class 1 dropped three balls. Why did they drop every ball from the same height?
questions.model_answer: To make it a fair test. The height was the same for every ball.
questions.explanation: If one ball was dropped from higher up, we could not tell why it bounced higher. Keeping the height the same makes the test fair.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Match each science step to an example.
pairs: I think the big stone will sink.
questions.explanation: A question starts an investigation. A prediction is a guess before the test. We record what we see and then share it.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Class 1 dropped balls from the same height. Bounce in hand spans: rubber ball 6, tennis ball 4, football 3. The ___ bounced the lowest.
questions.explanation: The football has the smallest number, 3, so it bounced the lowest. The rubber ball bounced highest with 6.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Class 1 dropped balls from the same height. Bounce in hand spans: rubber ball 6, tennis ball 4, football 3. How much higher did the rubber ball bounce than the tennis ball?
questions.explanation: 6 take away 4 is 2. The rubber ball bounced 2 hand spans higher than the tennis ball.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Tuli tests two paper planes. She throws plane A very hard and plane B gently. Plane A flies further. What should she change?
options: Throw plane B even more gently.
Throw both planes in the same way.
questions.explanation: Tuli threw the planes differently, so we cannot tell if the plane or the throw made the difference. Throwing both the same way makes it fair.

questions.title: Young Scientists
questions.stem: Joy grows two bean plants in the same kind of pot. Plant A is in the sun and gets water. Plant B is in a dark cupboard and gets no water. Which things are different? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: The water and the light are different. Because two things changed, Joy cannot tell which one made plant B small. A fair test changes only one thing.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Which one is a living thing?
questions.explanation: A goat is alive. It eats, grows and has young. A stone, a bicycle and a chair are never alive.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Sort the pictures into living and non-living.
questions.explanation: Worms, flowers and goats grow, feed and have young, so they are living. A teddy bear, a bicycle and a stone are non-living.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Living things need food, air and ___ to stay alive.
questions.explanation: All living things need water. Food, water and air keep them alive.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: A mango tree is not alive because it cannot walk.
questions.explanation: A mango tree is alive. It grows, takes in water through its roots and makes seeds. Plants do not need to walk to be alive.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: A toy car is alive because it moves.
questions.explanation: A car can move, but it cannot grow, feed or have young. Things that only move are not alive.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: What do living things do? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: Living things grow, have young and need food. Wheels and batteries belong to machines, not to living things.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Match each picture to what a living thing needs.
questions.explanation: Living things need food, water, light and warmth, and a safe place to live (shelter).

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Living things grow and change. Put these pictures in order from youngest to oldest.
questions.explanation: A person starts as a baby, grows into a child, then an adult, and later becomes an older person.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Which thing do all living things do?
questions.explanation: All living things grow. Not all of them talk or fly.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Raju's toy robot can move and make sounds. Is it alive?
options: No. It cannot grow, eat or have young.
questions.explanation: A robot can move and make sounds, but it does not grow, eat or have young. So it is not alive.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Sort these. Which ones do living things need?
questions.explanation: Living things need food, water, air and shelter to stay alive. They can live without toys, sweets or a television.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Class 1 watered one plate of bean seeds. They kept another plate dry. After one week, 9 seeds grew on the wet plate and ___ seeds grew on the dry plate.
questions.explanation: No seeds grew on the dry plate. The seeds needed water to start growing.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Arif finds a stone by the river. It rolled down the hill, so he thinks it is alive. Which question helps him most?
questions.explanation: Living things eat and grow. A stone has no food, never grows and cannot have babies. Water pushed it, so it only moved.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Sumi forgot to give her pot plant ___ for a week. Its leaves are drooping.
questions.explanation: Plants need water. Without it the leaves droop. Sumi should water her plant.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Imran keeps a pet goat. What must he give it? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: A goat needs food, water and a shelter to stay safe and warm. A toy car and a bicycle are things it does not need.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Joy has a small pot plant. Where should he put it so that it grows well?
questions.explanation: Plants need light and warmth to grow well. A sunny window sill gives them both.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Look at the four plants. What happens to a plant that has no water?
questions.image_alt: Four potted plants: one healthy, one wilted with no water, one pale with no light and one small because it is too cold.
questions.explanation: The plant with no water droops. The plant with no light turns pale. The plant that is too cold stays small.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Which pictures show living things? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: A cat, a butterfly and a rice plant are alive. They grow and need food. A chair and a bicycle are made by people and are never alive.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Look at the picture. A chick grows into a hen.
questions.image_alt: Life cycle of a chicken: egg, hatching, chick, adult hen.
questions.explanation: The picture shows an egg, then a chick, then an adult hen. Living things grow and change.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Mina tests if bean seeds need water. Which test is fair?
options: One plate wet on the window sill. One plate dry in a dark cupboard.
One plate wet on the window sill. One plate dry on the same window sill.
Both plates wet on the window sill.
questions.explanation: In a fair test only one thing changes. Both plates sit in the same place, and only the water is different. In the first test, the light changes too.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Look at this list: cat, chair, mango tree, stone, snail, bicycle. How many living things are in it?
questions.explanation: The cat, the mango tree and the snail are living. The chair, the stone and the bicycle are non-living. That makes 3.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Mina thinks a toy car is alive because it moves. Tell one thing a living thing does that a car cannot do.
questions.model_answer: A living thing can grow, eat or have young. A car cannot.
questions.explanation: Living things grow, eat, breathe and have young. A car cannot do any of these, so it is not alive.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: Put the steps in order to grow a bean plant.
sequence: Plant a bean seed in soil.
Water the soil every day.
A tiny shoot comes up.
The shoot grows into a bean plant.
questions.explanation: A seed needs water to start growing. First a shoot comes up, then it grows into a plant.

questions.title: Living Things and What They Need
questions.stem: In the seed test, 9 seeds grew on the wet plate and 0 on the dry plate. What does the test show?
questions.explanation: Only the water was different between the plates, so the test shows that seeds need water. It did not test soil or music.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: Match each animal to its home.
questions.explanation: A fish lives in water and a monkey lives in trees. An earthworm lives under the ground. A bird flies in the sky.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: An animal that lives in trees is…
questions.explanation: Arboreal means living in trees. Aquatic means living in water. Fossorial means living under the ground.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: A habitat is the ___ of a plant or an animal.
questions.explanation: A habitat is the home of a living thing. It gives food, water, air and shelter.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: A fish can live on dry land.
questions.explanation: A fish needs water to breathe and swim. Its habitat is a pond, a river or the sea.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: Where does each animal live? Sort them.
questions.explanation: Fish and frogs live in water. Monkeys and parrots live in trees. Earthworms and rats dig and live under the ground.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: Which animals are aquatic? They live in water. Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: Crabs, frogs, ducks and fish all live in or near water. A cow lives on the land and a monkey lives in trees.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: Put the homes in order from the highest to the lowest.
sequence: in the sky
in a tree
on the ground
under the ground
questions.explanation: Birds fly in the sky. Monkeys live in trees. Cows walk on the ground. Earthworms live under the ground.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
pairs: the home of a living thing
questions.explanation: These five words help us name where animals live.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: How does a pond help a frog?
options: Water to swim in and insects to eat.
Branches to climb and sleep on.
Soil to dig a tunnel in.
questions.explanation: A pond gives a frog water to swim in, insects to eat and plants to hide under. Climbing branches is what a monkey needs.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: Birds, bats and butterflies live in the sky. This is the ___ habitat.
questions.explanation: Aerial means in the air and sky. Birds, bats and butterflies fly there.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: A habitat gives a living thing food, water, air and shelter.
questions.explanation: A good habitat meets all the needs of the plants and animals that live there.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: Look at the pond. Which number is the frog?
questions.image_alt: A pond with the Sun, air and clouds, a duck, a fish, water, a rock, water plants and a frog, each with a number.
questions.explanation: Number 8 is the frog. Number 4 is the fish, 7 is the water plants and 2 is the air and clouds.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: Look at the pond. Which numbers show animals? Choose all that are right.
questions.image_alt: A pond with the Sun, air and clouds, a duck, a fish, water, a rock, water plants and a frog, each with a number.
questions.explanation: Number 3 is a duck, 4 is a fish and 8 is a frog. Number 5 is water and 6 is a rock, so they are not animals.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: Look at the Sundarbans tree. What are its roots standing in?
questions.image_alt: A mangrove tree with breathing roots and prop roots in salty mud.
questions.explanation: Mangrove trees in the Sundarbans grow in salty mud. Their roots stand in the mud and hold the tree up.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: Tuli goes by boat in the haor in Sylhet. She sees many fish and ducks. What kind of habitat is this?
questions.explanation: A haor is a big wetland full of water. Fish and ducks live there, so it is an aquatic habitat.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: Anika visits a pond with her class to count the animals. What is the safe way?
options: Reach into the water to catch them.
Look with her teacher and do not touch.
questions.explanation: We look, count and do not touch. Staying with a grown-up near water keeps us safe and does not harm the animals.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: Moung wants to see an earthworm in the garden. Where should he look?
options: in the soil under a stone
questions.explanation: Earthworms live in the soil under the ground. They are fossorial animals.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: The Sundarbans has land, trees, water, holes in the mud and sky. It has every kind of habitat.
questions.explanation: Tigers and deer walk on land. Monkeys climb trees. Fish and crocodiles swim in the rivers. Crabs dig holes in the mud. Birds fly above.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: Why can a fish not live in a tree?
questions.model_answer: A fish needs water to breathe and swim. A tree has no water.
questions.explanation: A fish needs water to breathe and swim. A tree is a habitat for monkeys and parrots, not for fish.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: Crabs dig holes in the mud in the Sundarbans. A hole under the ground is a ___ habitat.
questions.explanation: Fossorial means living under the ground. Crabs, earthworms and rats use holes in the ground.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: Anika sees a monkey eating fruit in a tree. What does the tree give the monkey? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: A tree gives a monkey fruit to eat, branches to climb and a place to sleep. A monkey does not swim or dig.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: Class 1 counted animals in 5 minutes. Pond: 4 frogs and 6 fish. Garden: 9 ants and 3 butterflies. Which place had more animals?
questions.explanation: The pond had 4 + 6 = 10 animals. The garden had 9 + 3 = 12 animals. The garden had 2 more.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: A kingfisher sits on a branch by a pond. It flies over the water and dives in to catch a fish. Which habitats does it use? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: The kingfisher flies in the sky, rests in a tree and hunts in the pond. It does not live under the ground.

questions.title: Habitats of Bangladesh
questions.stem: Ants walk on the land and dig homes in the soil. Which two words fit their habitats?
questions.explanation: Terrestrial means on land and fossorial means under the ground. An animal can live in more than one habitat.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Which food helps your body grow?
questions.explanation: An egg is a body-building food. It helps you grow. Fish, dal and milk help you grow too.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Which foods should we eat often? Which only a little?
questions.explanation: Rice, eggs and green vegetables give us energy, help us grow and keep us healthy. Sweets, chips and doughnuts are fine only as a small treat.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: A balanced diet has some of each kind of food and plenty of ___.
questions.explanation: We need to drink plenty of water every day, as well as eating different kinds of food.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Washing your hands with soap gets rid of germs.
questions.explanation: Soap and water wash germs off your hands. Clean hands help stop you getting ill.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: A fizzy drink is the best drink for a healthy body.
questions.explanation: Water is the best drink for your body. Fizzy drinks are full of sugar and do not help you grow.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: How can you keep your body healthy? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: Exercise, clean hands and clean teeth keep us healthy. We also need plenty of sleep and many kinds of food, not only sweets.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Match each picture to what it does for your body.
questions.explanation: Rice and roti give us energy. Fish, egg and dal help us grow. Fruit and vegetables protect us. We also drink plenty of water.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Children need to sleep about ___ hours every night.
questions.explanation: Children need about 10 hours of sleep. Sleep rests the body and helps us feel good the next day.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Put the steps for washing hands in order.
sequence: Wet your hands.
Rub soap on your hands.
Rub for 20 seconds.
Rinse off the soap.
Dry your hands.
questions.explanation: Wet your hands first, then use soap and rub for 20 seconds. Rinse the soap away and dry your hands last.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Which meal is the most balanced?
options: chips, a sweet cake and a fizzy drink
questions.explanation: Rice gives energy, fish helps us grow, spinach keeps us healthy, and water is the best drink. The other meals have no body-building or protecting foods.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Rice and roti give us ___.
questions.explanation: Rice, roti and potato are energy foods. They give us the energy to play and learn.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Class 1 put pretend germs (glitter) on their hands, then washed. Spots left: water 5 seconds, 30. Water 20 seconds, 15. Soap 20 seconds, 2. Which way cleaned best?
questions.explanation: Fewer spots mean cleaner hands. Soap for 20 seconds left only 2 spots, so it cleaned best.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Which food helps protect your body and keeps you healthy?
questions.explanation: Green vegetables and fruit have vitamins and fibre. They protect us and keep us healthy.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Which pictures show healthy habits? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: Washing with soap, running and brushing your teeth keep you healthy. Sweets and doughnuts are only for a small treat.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Match each picture to why it helps.
questions.explanation: Soap removes germs, brushing cleans teeth, sleep rests the body and running makes muscles strong.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Rafi's lunch is chips, a sweet cake and a fizzy drink. What should he change?
options: Drink water and add a banana.
questions.explanation: Water is a better drink, and a banana is a protecting food. Rafi also needs foods that help him grow, such as rice, dal or fish.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Tumpa watched cartoons until late. At school she is sleepy. What should she do tonight?
questions.explanation: Her body needs sleep. Going to bed early helps her feel awake and ready to play at school.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Mina has been playing football in the mud. Now it is time to eat lunch. What should she do first?
options: Wash her hands with soap and water.
Wipe her hands on her shirt.
questions.explanation: Muddy hands can carry germs. Washing with soap and water before eating helps keep us well.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Anika feels grumpy after a long day. Resting or playing with friends can help her feel better.
questions.explanation: Rest and fun help our bodies and our feelings. Playing with friends and relaxing keep us happy and well.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Anika wants to be active every day. What can she do? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: Walking, playing cricket and skipping make our bodies move and grow strong. Sitting or lying down all day does not.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Tumpa feels tired at school. Give her one tip to feel better.
questions.model_answer: Go to bed early, or eat a good breakfast, or play outside.
questions.explanation: A tired body needs sleep, good food and exercise. Any of these tips can help Tumpa feel better.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Nadia's dinner is rice, roti and potato. What should she add to make it balanced?
questions.explanation: Rice, roti and potato are all energy foods. Fish helps her grow and spinach protects her, so she needs both.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: In the glitter test, water for 5 seconds left 30 spots. Soap for 20 seconds left 2 spots. How many fewer spots did soap for 20 seconds leave?
questions.explanation: 30 take away 2 is 28. Soap for 20 seconds took away 28 more spots than water for 5 seconds.

questions.title: Healthy Bodies
questions.stem: Water for 5 seconds left 30 glitter spots. Soap for 20 seconds left 2 spots. Sumi says: 'They clean just as well.' Is Sumi right?
questions.explanation: 30 spots is much more than 2 spots. Soap and 20 seconds cleaned much better than a quick rinse.

questions.title: The Sun, Moon and Stars
questions.stem: Look at the stick and its shadow. When is the shadow shortest?
questions.image_alt: A stick and its shadow in the morning, at midday and in the evening as the Sun moves across the sky.
questions.explanation: At midday the Sun is high in the sky, so the shadow is short. In the morning and evening the Sun is low and the shadow is long.

questions.title: The Sun, Moon and Stars
questions.stem: Look at the picture. The stick's shadow is long in the morning and in the evening.
questions.image_alt: A stick and its shadow in the morning, at midday and in the evening as the Sun moves across the sky.
questions.explanation: When the Sun is low in the sky, shadows are long. This happens in the morning and the evening.

questions.title: The Sun, Moon and Stars
questions.stem: Look at the spinning Earth. The side facing the Sun has day.
questions.image_alt: The Sun lights one half of the spinning Earth: day on the side facing the Sun, night on the other side.
questions.explanation: The side of the Earth facing the Sun has day. The side facing away from the Sun has night.

questions.title: The Sun, Moon and Stars
questions.stem: Look at the Moon's shapes. Which number is the full Moon?
questions.image_alt: Eight shapes of the Moon numbered 1 to 8. Number 1 is the new Moon and number 5 is the full Moon.
questions.explanation: Number 5 is the full Moon, round and bright. Number 1 is the new Moon, when we can hardly see it.

questions.title: The Sun, Moon and Stars
questions.stem: What do we see in the sky by day? What do we see by night?
